label: conj:tempered-classification
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{conj:tempered-classification}
	Let $\pi$ be an irreducible tempered representation of $G_n$. Then $\pi$ is
	$H_n$-distinguished if and only if there exist integers
	$m_1,\ldots,m_k\geq 0$ and unitary $H_{r_i}$-distinguished supercuspidal
	representations
	\[
	\rho_i\in\mathcal D_{r_i},
	\qquad 1\leq i\leq k,
	\]
	such that
	\[
	\pi
	\simeq
	\mathcal B_{m_1}(\rho_1)
	\times\cdots\times
	\mathcal B_{m_k}(\rho_k),
	\]
	with
	\[
	\sum_{i=1}^k (2m_i+1)r_i=n.
	\]
	Equivalently, every irreducible tempered $H_n$-distinguished representation
	is obtained by parabolic induction from blocks of the form
	\[
	\rho
	\qquad\text{or}\qquad
	\delta_{m+1}(\rho)\times\delta_m(\rho),
	\]
	where $\rho$ is a unitary distinguished supercuspidal representation.
head: environment

label: lem:two-block-jacquet
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Two-block Jacquet module

title: Proof
body_md:
The centered segment defining $\delta_m(\rho)$ is
$
 \left[-\frac{m-1}{2},\frac{m-1}{2}\right]_\rho.
$
For the Levi of type $(ad,(m-a)d)$, the segment Jacquet-module formula cuts
this segment into consecutive pieces of lengths $a$ and $m-a$. Their
centers are $(m-a)/2$ and $-a/2$, respectively. Since
$\nu_\rho=\nu^s$, this gives \eqref{eq:general-two-block-jacquet}. The
vanishing assertion follows from the fact that every cuspidal atom on the
$\rho$-line has rank $d$; see \cite[\S2.4]{SharmaVerma2026} and
\cite{DeligneKazhdanVigneras1984,Tadic1990}.
head: environment

label: def:good-orbit
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:good-orbit}
The orbit
\[
   Py_iH_n
   \quad\text{or, equivalently,}\quad
   P\cdot(y_iH_n)\subset X_n
\]
is called a good orbit for $\sigma$ if
\begin{equation}\label{eq:def-good-orbit}
   \operatorname{Hom}_{H_n}
   \left(
      \mathcal V_i/\mathcal V_{i-1},
      \mathbb C
   \right)
   \neq0.
\end{equation}
head: environment
name: Good orbit

label: lem:dist-implies-good
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:dist-implies-good}
If
$\operatorname{Hom}_{H_n}\bigl(I_P(\sigma),\mathbb C\bigr)\neq0,$
then at least one orbit in $P\backslash G_n/H_n$ is good for $\sigma$.
head: environment
name: Distinction forces a good orbit

title: Proof
body_md:
Let
\[
   0\neq\ell\in\operatorname{Hom}_{H_n}(\mathcal V,\mathbb C).
\]
Choose the smallest $i$ for which
$ \ell|_{\mathcal V_i}\neq0.$ Then $\ell$ vanishes on $\mathcal V_{i-1}$ and therefore induces a nonzero
$H_n$-invariant functional on
$\mathcal V_i/\mathcal V_{i-1}$.
head: environment

label: rem:good-not-sufficient
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:good-not-sufficient}
The converse of Lemma~\ref{lem:dist-implies-good} is not automatic. A good
orbit gives an invariant functional on a graded piece, and such a functional
need not extend to the whole induced representation. One situation in
which the direction can be reversed is a closed orbit occurring as the final
quotient of \eqref{eq:mackey-good-filtration}: a functional on that quotient
pulls back to the whole representation.
head: environment
name: A good orbit is only a necessary condition in general

label: prop:good-orbit-general
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:good-orbit-general}
For a fixed orbit and its associated data $(\beta,\tau)$, the corresponding
graded piece can contribute an $H_n$-invariant functional only if
$r_{L,M_\alpha}(\sigma)$ has an irreducible constituent
\eqref{eq:jacquet-constituent-good} satisfying:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item if
$(i,j)\prec\tau(i,j),$
then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:nu-pair-good}
	\eta_{i,j}\simeq \nu\,\eta_{\tau(i,j)}.
\end{equation}
\item if
$ \tau(i,j)=(i,j),$
then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fixed-good}
	\operatorname{Hom}_{H_{n_{i,j}}}(\eta_{i,j},\mathbb C)\neq0.
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
If the normalized Jacquet module
$r_{L,M_\alpha}(\sigma)$ is itself irreducible, then these two conditions,
together with \eqref{eq:ordering-restriction}, are equivalent to the orbit
being good.
head: environment
name: Representation-theoretic good-orbit criterion

title: Proof
body_md:
For the orbit represented by $x$, Proposition~4.1 of \cite{SharmaVerma2026}, following
\cite[Proposition~4.1]{Offen2017}, identifies the Hom-space of the graded piece with
\[
   \operatorname{Hom}_{L_x}
   \left(
      r_{L,M_\alpha}(\sigma),
      \delta_{Q_x}\delta_Q^{-1/2}
   \right).
\]
Proposition~4.2 of \cite{SharmaVerma2026}, using the orbit description of
\cite{Offen2017}, evaluates this Hom-space on an
irreducible tensor representation and gives exactly
\eqref{eq:nu-pair-good} and \eqref{eq:fixed-good}. The ordering condition
\eqref{eq:ordering-restriction} is the orbit condition from
\cite[\S3.3]{SharmaVerma2026}; compare \cite[Lemma~3.2]{Offen2017}. If the
Jacquet module is irreducible, no
passage to another constituent is necessary, and the criterion is an
equivalence.
head: environment

label: def:combinatorial-good
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:combinatorial-good}
The segment decomposition
\eqref{eq:segment-good-decomposition}, together with the orbit involution
$\tau$, is called \emph{combinatorially good} if:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(C\arabic*)}]
\item
$ \tau(i,j+1)\ll\tau(i,j)
   \qquad(1\leq j<k_i);$

\item for every two-cycle, oriented by
$(i,j)\prec\tau(i,j)$,
$
   Q(\Delta_{i,j})
   \simeq
   \nu\,Q(\Delta_{\tau(i,j)});
$
\item for every fixed point,
$
   Q(\Delta_{i,j})
   \quad\text{is }H_{n_{i,j}}\text{-distinguished}.
$
\end{enumerate}
head: environment
name: Combinatorially good segment data

label: cor:good-combinatorial
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:good-combinatorial}
Let
\[
   \sigma
   =
   Q(\Delta_1)\otimes\cdots\otimes Q(\Delta_t).
\]
For a fixed $P_\alpha$-orbit whose Jacquet refinement is nonzero, the orbit
is good for $\sigma$ if and only if its associated segment data are
combinatorially good in the sense of
Definition~\ref{def:combinatorial-good}.
head: environment
name: Good orbit $\Longleftrightarrow$ combinatorially good data

title: Proof
body_md:
By \eqref{eq:segment-good-jacquet}, the relevant normalized Jacquet module is
the single irreducible tensor product
\[
   \mathop{\otimes}_{(i,j)}
   Q(\Delta_{i,j}).
\]
The result is therefore the irreducible case of
Proposition~\ref{prop:good-orbit-general}.
head: environment

label: conj:prasad-ds
title: Conjecture
body_md:
\label{conj:prasad-ds}
Let $\delta$ be an irreducible discrete-series representation of $G_n$ and
write its Weil--Deligne parameter in the form
\[
   \phi_\delta=\tau\otimes S_a,
\]
where $\tau$ is an irreducible representation of $W_F$ and $S_a$ is the
$a$-dimensional irreducible representation of $\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb C)$. Then $\delta$
is $H_n$-distinguished if and only if $\delta$ is supercuspidal,
$\tau$ is odd-dimensional, and
  $ a=2.$
head: environment
name: Prasad's discrete-series conjecture

label: thm:ds
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:ds}
Let $\delta$ be an irreducible discrete-series representation of $G_n$.
Then
\[
 \operatorname{Hom}_{H_n}(\delta,\mathbb C)\neq0
\]
if and only if $\delta$ is supercuspidal and its Jacquet--Langlands transfer
$\operatorname{JL}(\delta)$ to $\operatorname{GL}_{2n}(F)$ is non-supercuspidal.
Equivalently, the distinguished discrete-series representations are exactly
the supercuspidal representations predicted by
Conjecture~\ref{conj:prasad-ds}. See \cite[Corollary~1.4]{Matringe2026}; and
\cite{MSSS2026}.
head: environment
name: Discrete-series distinction

label: def:block
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:block}
Let $\rho\in\mathcal D_r$. Put
\[
 \mathcal B_0(\rho)=\rho.
\]
For $m\geq1$, define
\begin{equation}\label{eq:block}
 \mathcal B_m(\rho)
 :=
 \delta_{m+1}(\rho)\times\delta_m(\rho).
\end{equation}
Thus $\mathcal B_m(\rho)$ is a representation of
$ G_{(2m+1)r}.$
head: environment
name: Elementary tempered blocks

label: lem:block-temp
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Both factors in \eqref{eq:block} are unitary discrete-series
representations. Their defining centered segments are nested, hence are not
linked. The irreducibility criterion for products of segment
representations therefore gives the irreducibility of
$\delta_{m+1}(\rho)\times\delta_m(\rho)$. Since it is a normalized
parabolic induction of unitary discrete-series representations, it is
tempered, see \cite[Corollary 6.3]{Tadic2015}.
head: environment

label: conj:block
title: Conjecture
body_md:
\label{conj:block}
Let $\pi\in\operatorname{Irr}(G_n)$ be tempered. Then
$
 \operatorname{Hom}_{H_n}(\pi,\mathbb C)\neq0
$
if and only if
\[
 \pi
 \simeq
 \mathcal B_{m_1}(\rho_1)
 \times\cdots\times
 \mathcal B_{m_t}(\rho_t),
\]
where $\rho_i\in\mathcal D$ and $m_i\geq0$ for every $i$.
head: environment
name: Prasad's revised tempered distinction conjecture: block form

title: Remark
body_md:
Section~\ref{sec:Bm-general} proves the ``if'' direction of
Conjecture~\ref{conj:block} in arbitrary rank: every elementary block
$\mathcal B_m(\rho)$ is distinguished, and arbitrary products of such blocks are
distinguished by the hereditary property. The substantive remaining
content is the converse assertion that no other tempered connected
component can occur.
head: environment

label: conj:param
title: Conjecture
body_md:
\label{conj:param}
Let $\pi$ be an irreducible tempered representation of $G_n$. Then $\pi$
is $H_n$-distinguished if and only if its parameter is a direct sum of
pieces of the following two types:
\begin{align*}
 &\tau\otimes S_2,\\
 &\tau\otimes\left(S_{2m}\oplus S_{2m+2}\right),
 \qquad m\geq1,
\end{align*}
where in each case $\tau\otimes S_2$ is the parameter of a distinguished
supercuspidal representation of some $G_r$.
head: environment
name: Tempered distinction: parameter form

title: Proposition
body_md: Conjectures~\ref{conj:block} and \ref{conj:param} are equivalent.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
This follows from \eqref{eq:rho-param}, \eqref{eq:delta-param}, additivity of
Langlands parameters under tempered parabolic induction, and
\[
 S_{2m+1}\otimes S_2
 \simeq
 S_{2m+2}\oplus S_{2m}.
\]
head: environment

label: rem:adj
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:adj}
For a distinguished supercuspidal $\rho$, the reducibility step is
$s(\rho)=2$. Thus the cuspidal support of $\delta_m(\rho)$, in
$\nu$-exponents, is
$
 \{1-m,3-m,\ldots,m-3,m-1\}.
$
The two supports
$
 \operatorname{Supp}(\delta_{m+1}(\rho))
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \operatorname{Supp}(\delta_m(\rho))
$
are the two parity classes in the consecutive interval
$
 \{-m,-m+1,\ldots,m-1,m\}.
$
This is the local combinatorial reason for the occurrence of adjacent
lengths.
head: environment
name: Parameter interpretation

label: lem:closed-general
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:closed-general}
Suppose that
$ r_{(d,k),(d+k)}(\lambda_2)
$
contains an irreducible constituent
$
   \eta_0\otimes\eta_2,
   \qquad
   \eta_0\in\operatorname{Irr}(G_d),\quad
   \eta_2\in\operatorname{Irr}(G_k).
$
Then the constituent
$
   \lambda_1\otimes\eta_0\otimes\eta_2
$
contributes to the closed-orbit Hom-space in
\eqref{eq:closed-Hom-general} provided
\begin{equation}\label{eq:closed-two-conditions}
   \lambda_1\simeq\nu\eta_2
   \qquad\text{and}\qquad
   \operatorname{Hom}_{H_d}(\eta_0,\mathbb C)\neq0.
\end{equation}
head: environment
name: Closed-orbit pairing criterion

title: Proof
body_md:
For the closed orbit the involution on the three refined Levi blocks exchanges
the two $G_k$-blocks and fixes the middle $G_d$-block. Proposition~4.2 of \cite{SharmaVerma2026}, with the orbit description of
\cite{Offen2017}, gives the two conditions in
\eqref{eq:closed-two-conditions}.
head: environment

label: thm:Bm-general
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:Bm-general}
Let $\rho\in\mathcal D_d$ be a unitary distinguished supercuspidal representation of
$G_d$, and let $m\geq1$. Then
\[
   \mathcal B_m(\rho)
   =
   \delta_{m+1}(\rho)\times\delta_m(\rho)
\]
admits a symplectic model. Equivalently,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Bm-distinguished-general}
   \operatorname{Hom}_{H_{(2m+1)d}}
   \left(
      \mathcal B_m(\rho),\mathbb C
   \right)
   \neq0.
\end{equation}
head: environment
name: Existence of the elementary blocks

title: Proof
body_md:
Consider the irreducible induced representation $\Pi_m$ in
\eqref{eq:Bm-induced}. By \eqref{eq:Bm-irred}, it is isomorphic to
$\mathcal B_m(\rho)$.
We use the closed orbit $O_k$ in
\[
   P_{md,(m+1)d}\backslash G_{(2m+1)d}/H_{(2m+1)d}.
\]
By \eqref{eq:jacquet-Bm-master}, the relevant Jacquet-module constituent of
the second inducing factor is
$ \nu^m\rho
   \otimes
   \nu^{-1}\delta_m(\rho).
$
Thus the three refined factors attached to the closed orbit are
$
   \delta_m(\rho)
   \otimes
   \nu^m\rho
   \otimes
   \nu^{-1}\delta_m(\rho).
$
The two exchanged $G_{md}$-factors satisfy
$  \delta_m(\rho)
   =
   \nu\bigl(\nu^{-1}\delta_m(\rho)\bigr).$
Moreover,
$
   \operatorname{Hom}_{H_d}(\nu^m\rho,\mathbb C)
   =
   \operatorname{Hom}_{H_d}(\rho,\mathbb C)
   \neq0,
$
because $\nu$ is trivial on $H_d$. Therefore
Lemma~\ref{lem:closed-general} implies that the closed-orbit quotient has a
nonzero $H_n$-invariant linear form:
\[
   \operatorname{Hom}_{H_n}
   \left(
      \text{closed-orbit quotient of }\Pi_m|_{H_n},
      \mathbb C
   \right)
   \neq0.
\]

Since $O_k$ is closed, its term is the final quotient in the geometric-lemma
filtration. Hence there is a canonical $H_n$-equivariant surjection
\[
   \Pi_m|_{H_n}
   \twoheadrightarrow
   \text{closed-orbit quotient}.
\]
Pulling back a nonzero invariant form through this surjection gives a
nonzero element of
$\operatorname{Hom}_{H_n}(\Pi_m,\mathbb C).
$
Finally $\Pi_m\simeq\mathcal B_m(\rho)$, so
\eqref{eq:Bm-distinguished-general} follows.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
The refined Levi for the closed orbit has three blocks of ranks
$md,\quad d,\quad md.
$
The corresponding involution is
$
   1\longleftrightarrow3,
   \qquad
   2\longmapsto2.
$
Thus the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:Bm-general} is represented by the
$
   \delta_m(\rho)
   \quad\longleftrightarrow\quad
   \nu^{-1}\delta_m(\rho),
   \qquad
   \nu^m\rho\ \text{fixed}.
$
The $\nu$-pairing of the first two factors comes from the modulus character
of the closed orbit, whereas the fixed factor survives because the
supercuspidal representation $\rho$ is itself distinguished.
head: environment
name: The orbit involution

title: Remark
body_md:
Section~5.2 of \cite{SharmaVerma2026}, using the symplectic-multiset
argument of \cite{MitraOffenSayag2017}, treats a supercuspidal line generated
by a representation which does not have a symplectic model. There a good
decomposition has no fixed points: every refined segment must occur in a
$\nu$-paired two-cycle. Theorem~\ref{thm:Bm-general} shows what changes on a distinguished
supercuspidal line. A single fixed piece,
namely $\nu^m\rho$, is now allowed, and the remainder of
$\delta_{m+1}(\rho)$ pairs with the external factor
$\delta_m(\rho)$.
head: environment
name: Comparison with the non-distinguished supercuspidal line

label: cor:if-tempered
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:if-tempered}
Let
\[
   \pi
   =
   \mathcal B_{m_1}(\rho_1)
   \times\cdots\times
   \mathcal B_{m_t}(\rho_t),
\]
where $\rho_i\in\mathcal D$ and $m_i\geq0$. Then $\pi$ has a symplectic model.
head: environment
name: The ``if'' direction of the tempered conjecture

title: Proof
body_md:
If $m_i=0$, then $\mathcal B_0(\rho_i)=\rho_i$ is distinguished by definition.
If $m_i\geq1$, then $\mathcal B_{m_i}(\rho_i)$ is distinguished by
Theorem~\ref{thm:Bm-general}. The hereditary property of the symplectic
model, \cite[Theorem~4.1]{SharmaVerma2026}, now gives the result; see also
\cite[Proposition~7.1]{Offen2017} and
\cite[Theorem~5.4]{MatringeOffenYang2024}.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
The converse, proved in Section~\ref{sec:converse}, shows that every
irreducible tempered distinguished representation is a product of the
blocks above.
head: environment

label: thm:rank5
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Tempered distinction for $G_5$

title: Remark
body_md:
Theorem~\ref{thm:rank5} follows from the general classification, Theorem~\ref{thm:main-classification}, proved in
Section~\ref{sec:converse}. Indeed, an elementary block
$\mathcal B_m(\rho)$ has rank $(2m+1)r$ when $\rho\in\mathcal D_r$. In total rank five,
a non-supercuspidal block therefore has $r=1$ and is either
$\mathcal B_1(\chi)$ or $\mathcal B_2(\chi)$; the remaining rank is filled by
distinguished supercuspidal singletons.
head: environment

label: lem:maximal-factor-jacquet
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:maximal-factor-jacquet}
Let $\rho\in\mathcal D_d$ and $L\ge2$. For $0<t<L$,
\[
 r_{(td,(L-t)d),(Ld)}\bigl(\delta_L(\rho)\bigr)
 =
 \nu^{L-t}\delta_t(\rho)
 \otimes
 \nu^{-t}\delta_{L-t}(\rho).
\]
head: environment
name: Jacquet module of the maximal factor

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $\rho$ is distinguished, $s(\rho)=2$. The assertion is therefore the
specialization of \eqref{eq:maximal-jacquet-deltaL} to $s(\rho)=2$.
head: environment

label: rem:terminal-piece-shape
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:terminal-piece-shape}
Let
$   \sigma
   =
   \delta_{K_1}(\rho_1)\times\cdots\times\delta_{K_u}(\rho_u)
$
be tempered, and consider a Jacquet-module constituent
$ S\otimes T
   \quad\text{of}\quad
   r_{(N-r,r),(N)}(\sigma).
$
Suppose that $T$ lies on the cuspidal line of a unitary supercuspidal
representation $\rho$, and write $s=s(\rho)$.

The possible contribution to $T$ can be read from the endpoint of the
centered segment.
The representation $\delta_K(\rho)$ corresponds to the centered segment
\[
   \left[-\frac{K-1}{2},\frac{K-1}{2}\right]_\rho .
\]
When a Jacquet module separates off a piece into the second Levi factor,
that piece is taken from the lower end of this segment. This is the usual
segment description of Jacquet modules; see, for example,
\cite{Tadic1990} and \cite[\S2.4]{SharmaVerma2026}. Thus, if
$\delta_K(\rho)$ contributes nontrivially to $T$, the contribution starts
at the left endpoint of the segment. Since $\nu_\rho=\nu^{s}$, this
endpoint is
\[
   -\frac{s(K-1)}{2}
\]
when written in ordinary $\nu$-exponents.

Thus the initial exponent of a terminal piece determines the length $K$ of
the discrete-series factor from which it comes. We use this below to compare
terminal Jacquet pieces with the contribution from $\delta_L(\rho)$.
head: environment
name: Terminal pieces of centered segments

label: rem:adjacent-terminal-rigidity
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:adjacent-terminal-rigidity}
	In the situation of Remark~\ref{rem:terminal-piece-shape}, assume that
	$s(\rho)=2$, every factor on the $\rho$-line has length at most $L$, and
	\[
	T\simeq\delta_{L-1}(\rho).
	\]
	Then $T$ must come from one whole original factor
	$\delta_{L-1}(\rho)$ of $\sigma$; it cannot be assembled from proper
	terminal pieces of several factors.
	
	Indeed, the support of $T$ runs from $2-L$ to $L-2$. If a centered factor
	$\delta_K(\rho)$ supplies the top exponent $L-2$, then its terminal piece
	starts at $1-K$. Since this starting point must still lie in the support of
	$T$, one has $K\le L-1$; on the other hand, reaching the exponent $L-2$
	forces $K\ge L-1$. Hence $K=L-1$. A proper terminal piece of
	$\delta_{L-1}(\rho)$ stops before $L-2$, so this factor must contribute its
	whole segment. Its rank is already $(L-1)d$, the full rank of $T$, and
	there is therefore no room for any additional contribution.
head: environment
name: Endpoint rigidity

label: prop:distinguished-cuspidal-support
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:distinguished-cuspidal-support}
	Every supercuspidal line occurring in the tempered support of an
	$H_n$-distinguished tempered representation contains a distinguished
	supercuspidal representation.
head: environment
name: Distinguished cuspidal support

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix a unitary supercuspidal representation $\rho$ whose line occurs in the
	tempered support, and choose $\delta_L(\rho)$ of maximal length on that
	line. Reorder the tempered induction as in
	\eqref{eq:general-temp-converse}. Suppose that $\rho$ is not distinguished.
	Then, by \cite[Remark~1.1]{SharmaVerma2026}, using the Jacquet--Langlands
	reducibility calculation of \cite[Theorem~B.2.b]{DeligneKazhdanVigneras1984},
	and the discrete-series
	distinction theorem,
$
	s(\rho)=1.
$
	Since $\pi$ is distinguished, Lemma~\ref{lem:dist-implies-good} gives a good
	orbit in the $P_{Ld,N}$-Mackey filtration. Write $r=td$.
	
	If $t=0$, the open-orbit condition requires
	\[
	\operatorname{Hom}_{H_{Ld}}(\delta_L(\rho),\mathbb C)\neq0.
	\]
	For $L=1$ this contradicts the assumption on $\rho$; for $L>1$ it
	contradicts Theorem~\ref{thm:ds}.
	
	Assume $0<t<L$. By \eqref{eq:maximal-three-conditions},
$
	B_t=\nu^{-t/2}\delta_{L-t}(\rho)
$
	is distinguished. Since $\nu$ is trivial on every $H_j$, this is equivalent
	to distinction of $\delta_{L-t}(\rho)$. If $L-t>1$, this contradicts the
	discrete-series distinction theorem; if $L-t=1$, it says that $\rho$ is
	distinguished. Thus no interior orbit can be good.
	
	It remains to exclude the full-pairing orbit $t=L$. If this orbit is
	available, Proposition~4.2 of \cite{SharmaVerma2026}, with the orbit
	analysis of \cite{Offen2017}, forces a terminal
	constituent $T$ of a Jacquet module of $\sigma$ with
	\[
	\delta_L(\rho)\simeq\nu T,
	\qquad\text{hence}\qquad
	T\simeq\nu^{-1}\delta_L(\rho).
	\]
	We now exclude this possibility directly. Since $s(\rho)=1$, the ordinary
	$\nu$-cuspidal support of $\delta_L(\rho)$ is
	\[
	\left\{
	\nu^{-(L-1)/2}\rho,\nu^{-(L-3)/2}\rho,\ldots,
	\nu^{(L-1)/2}\rho
	\right\}.
	\]
	Consequently
	\[
	\operatorname{cusp}\bigl(\nu^{-1}\delta_L(\rho)\bigr)
	=
	\left\{
	\nu^{-(L+1)/2}\rho,\nu^{-(L-1)/2}\rho,\ldots,
	\nu^{(L-3)/2}\rho
	\right\}.
	\]
	In particular, $\nu^{-(L+1)/2}\rho$ occurs in the cuspidal support of $T$,
	and therefore in the cuspidal support of $\sigma$. Because $\sigma$ is
	tempered, every discrete-series factor on the $\rho$-line is centered, say
	$\delta_K(\rho)$. Hence a factor containing
	$\nu^{-(L+1)/2}\rho$ also contains $\nu^{(L+1)/2}\rho$. Since the extreme
	ordinary exponents of $\delta_K(\rho)$ are
	\[
	-\frac{K-1}{2}\qquad\text{and}\qquad \frac{K-1}{2},
	\]
	we must have
	\[
	\frac{K-1}{2}\geq \frac{L+1}{2},
	\qquad\text{so}\qquad K\geq L+2.
	\]
	This contradicts the maximality of $L$ on the $\rho$-line. Thus the
	full-pairing orbit is not good either.
	
	All possible orbits have been excluded, contradicting
	Lemma~\ref{lem:dist-implies-good}. Hence $\rho$ is distinguished.
head: environment

label: lem:closed-orbit-maximality
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:closed-orbit-maximality}
Let $\rho\in\mathcal D_d$, let $L\geq1$, and let $\sigma$ be tempered. Assume that
$L$ is maximal among the lengths of the discrete-series factors occurring on
the $\rho$-cuspidal line in $\delta_L(\rho)\times\sigma$. Then no irreducible
constituent $T$ of a normalized Jacquet module of $\sigma$ can satisfy
\[
   T\simeq \nu^{-1}\delta_L(\rho).
\]
Consequently, in the maximal-parabolic Mackey filtration for
$\delta_L(\rho)\times\sigma$, the full-pairing (closed) orbit $r=Ld$ is not
good.
head: environment
name: Closed-orbit exclusion on a distinguished line

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $\rho$ is distinguished, $s(\rho)=2$. Hence the ordinary
$\nu$-cuspidal support of $\delta_L(\rho)$ is
\[
   \{\nu^{1-L}\rho,\nu^{3-L}\rho,\ldots,\nu^{L-1}\rho\},
\]
and therefore
\[
   \operatorname{cusp}\bigl(\nu^{-1}\delta_L(\rho)\bigr)
   =
   \{\nu^{-L}\rho,\nu^{2-L}\rho,\ldots,\nu^{L-2}\rho\}.
\]
In particular, if a Jacquet constituent $T$ of $\sigma$ were isomorphic to
$\nu^{-1}\delta_L(\rho)$, then $\nu^{-L}\rho$ would occur in the cuspidal
support of $T$, and hence in the cuspidal support of $\sigma$. Normalized
Jacquet functors do not create new supercuspidal support: the supercuspidal
support of every Jacquet constituent is obtained from the supercuspidal
support of the original representation.

Because $\sigma$ is tempered, every discrete-series factor on the
$\rho$-line is centered, say $\delta_K(\rho)$, with ordinary support
\[
   \{\nu^{1-K}\rho,\nu^{3-K}\rho,\ldots,\nu^{K-1}\rho\}.
\]
Thus, if $\nu^{-L}\rho$ occurs in the support of such a factor, symmetry of
the centered segment implies that $\nu^{L}\rho$ occurs in the same factor.
Equivalently, $K-1\geq L$, and hence $K\geq L+1$. This contradicts the
maximality of $L$.

For the closed orbit $r=Ld$, the whole factor $\delta_L(\rho)$ lies on the
diagonal $G_{Ld}$-part of the stabilizer. The good-orbit pairing condition
would therefore force
$
   \delta_L(\rho)\simeq \nu T,
   \qquad\text{hence}\qquad
   T\simeq\nu^{-1}\delta_L(\rho),
$
which has just been shown to be impossible. Thus the closed orbit cannot
contribute.
head: environment

label: prop:unique-orbit
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:unique-orbit}
Let $
   \pi=\delta_L(\rho)\times\sigma
$
be irreducible tempered and $H_n$-distinguished. Assume that
$\rho\in\mathcal D_d$, that $L\ge2$, and that $L$ is maximal among the lengths on
the $\rho$-line. Then every good orbit in the maximal-parabolic Mackey
filtration for $P_{Ld,N}$ has
\[
 r=(L-1)d.
\]
For a contributing irreducible subquotient
$S\otimes T$ of
$r_{(N-(L-1)d,(L-1)d),(N)}(\sigma)$ one has
$
  T\simeq\delta_{L-1}(\rho).
$
Consequently $\sigma$ contains a whole original factor
$\delta_{L-1}(\rho)$.
head: environment
name: The contributing orbit

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $\rho$ is distinguished, $s(\rho)=2$.

\emph{Step 1: exclude the open orbit and determine the interior orbit.}
The open orbit $r=0$ is not good, because it would require
$\delta_L(\rho)$ itself to be distinguished; this is impossible for
$L>1$ by Theorem~\ref{thm:ds}. Now let $r=td$ with $0<t<L$. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:maximal-factor-jacquet} and
\eqref{eq:maximal-three-conditions}, the fixed symplectic factor
\[
   \nu^{-t}\delta_{L-t}(\rho)
\]
must be distinguished. Since $\nu$ is trivial on the symplectic group,
this is equivalent to distinction of $\delta_{L-t}(\rho)$. Theorem
\ref{thm:ds} therefore forces
\[
   L-t=1.
\]
Hence the only possible interior good orbit is
$
  r=(L-1)d.
$

\emph{Step 2: exclude the full-pairing closed orbit.}
If $r=Ld$ is available, the whole factor $\delta_L(\rho)$ lies on the
diagonal $G_{Ld}$-part of the stabilizer. The diagonal pairing would force
\[
   \delta_L(\rho)\simeq\nu T,
   \qquad\text{hence}\qquad
   T\simeq\nu^{-1}\delta_L(\rho).
\]
Lemma~\ref{lem:closed-orbit-maximality} proves that this is impossible: it
would put $\nu^{-L}\rho$ in the cuspidal support of $\sigma$, and
centeredness of the tempered $\rho$-line factors would then force a factor
of length at least $L+1$, contradicting maximality. Thus $r=Ld$ does not
contribute.

\emph{Step 3: identify the terminal factor for the unique orbit.}
For $t=L-1$, Lemma~\ref{lem:maximal-factor-jacquet} gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:unique-jacquet}
   r_{((L-1)d,d),(Ld)}\bigl(\delta_L(\rho)\bigr)
   =
   \nu\delta_{L-1}(\rho)
   \otimes
   \nu^{-(L-1)}\rho.
\end{equation}
Let $S\otimes T$ be a contributing irreducible subquotient of
$
   r_{(N-(L-1)d,(L-1)d),(N)}(\sigma).
$
The diagonal $G_{(L-1)d}$-condition in
\eqref{eq:maximal-three-conditions} is
$
   \nu\delta_{L-1}(\rho)\simeq\nu T,
$
and therefore
$
  T\simeq\delta_{L-1}(\rho).
$

By endpoint rigidity, namely Remark~\ref{rem:adjacent-terminal-rigidity},
this $T$ is contributed by one whole original
$\delta_{L-1}(\rho)$-factor of $\sigma$ and by no other factor. In particular, $\sigma$ contains a whole original
factor $\delta_{L-1}(\rho)$.
head: environment

label: thm:rank-reduction
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:rank-reduction}
Let $
   \pi=\delta_L(\rho)\times\sigma
$
be irreducible tempered and $H_n$-distinguished, and suppose $L$ is maximal
among the lengths occurring on the $\rho$-line. Then $\rho$ is
distinguished. Moreover:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item if $L=1$, then $\sigma$ is distinguished;
\item if $L\ge2$, then, after reordering the tempered factors,
\[
   \sigma\simeq\delta_{L-1}(\rho)\times\pi_0
\]
with $
   \operatorname{Hom}_{H_{n-(2L-1)d}}(\pi_0,\mathbb C)\neq0.
$

Equivalently, $
   \pi\simeq\mathcal B_{L-1}(\rho)\times\pi_0
$
with $\pi_0$ tempered and distinguished.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment
name: Rank reduction

title: Proof
body_md:
Proposition~\ref{prop:distinguished-cuspidal-support} first shows that
$\rho$ is distinguished.

Suppose $L=1$. The only possible good orbit is the open orbit. Indeed, if
the full-pairing orbit is available, it would force a terminal constituent
$\nu^{-1}\rho$, excluded by Lemma~\ref{lem:closed-orbit-maximality}; if it
is not available, there is nothing to exclude. The open-orbit formula is
\[
   \operatorname{Hom}_{H_d}(\rho,\mathbb C)
   \otimes
   \operatorname{Hom}_{H_{n-d}}(\sigma,\mathbb C),
\]
and the first factor is nonzero. Hence $\sigma$ is distinguished.

Now assume $L\ge2$. We use the rank-reduction argument
\eqref{eq:rank-reduction-mechanism} step by step.

\emph{Step 1: the unique good orbit.}
By Proposition~\ref{prop:unique-orbit}, every good orbit has
\[ r=(L-1)d.
\]
The proof of that proposition includes the full exclusion of the closed
orbit $r=Ld$: its pairing would force
$\nu^{-1}\delta_L(\rho)$ in a Jacquet module of $\sigma$, hence
$\nu^{-L}\rho$ in the cuspidal support of $\sigma$, which by centeredness
would force a $\rho$-line factor of length at least $L+1$, contrary to the
maximality of $L$.

\emph{Step 2: the adjacent discrete-series factor occurs in the Jacquet
module of $\sigma$.}
Let
$
   S\otimes T
$
be a constituent of
\[
   r_{(n_0,(L-1)d)}(\sigma),
   \qquad n_0=n-(2L-1)d,
\]
selected by the good orbit. From \eqref{eq:unique-jacquet}, the
$G_{(L-1)d}$-part coming from $\delta_L(\rho)$ is
$\nu\delta_{L-1}(\rho)$. Hence the diagonal pairing gives
\[
   \nu\delta_{L-1}(\rho)\simeq\nu T,
\]
so
$ T\simeq\delta_{L-1}(\rho).
$

\emph{Step 3: $\delta_{L-1}(\rho)$ is a whole original factor of
$\sigma$.}
The ordinary $\nu$-support of $T=\delta_{L-1}(\rho)$ is
\[
   2-L,\ 4-L,\ldots,\ L-2.
\]
Choose an original $\rho$-line factor $\delta_K(\rho)$ of $\sigma$ whose
terminal Jacquet contribution supplies the top exponent $L-2$. Such a
terminal piece begins at $1-K$. Since all its exponents must lie in the
support of $T$, we have
\[
   1-K\ge2-L,
\]
so $K\le L-1$. On the other hand, in order to contain the top exponent
$L-2$ one must have
\[
   K-1\ge L-2,
\]
so $K\ge L-1$. Therefore
$
   K=L-1.
$

A proper lower terminal piece of $\delta_{L-1}(\rho)$ stops before the top
endpoint $L-2$. Hence this factor must contribute its whole centered
segment to $T$. Since its rank is already $(L-1)d$, the full rank of $T$,
no other original factor contributes to the terminal block. Thus, after
reordering,
\[  \sigma\simeq\delta_{L-1}(\rho)\times\pi_0
   \]
for a tempered representation $\pi_0\in\operatorname{Irr}(G_{n_0})$, and the complementary
Jacquet factor is
$ S\simeq\pi_0.
$

This is precisely the endpoint-rigidity observation of
Remark~\ref{rem:adjacent-terminal-rigidity} applied to the present good
orbit.

\emph{Step 4: the remainder $\pi_0$ is distinguished.}
For $r=(L-1)d$, the Levi part of the orbit stabilizer is
\[
   \Delta\bigl(G_{(L-1)d}\times G_{(L-1)d}\bigr)
   \times H_d\times H_{n_0}.
\]
The three good-orbit conditions are therefore
\[
   \nu\delta_{L-1}(\rho)\simeq\nu T,
   \qquad
   \operatorname{Hom}_{H_d}(\nu^{-(L-1)}\rho,\mathbb C)\neq0,
   \qquad
   \operatorname{Hom}_{H_{n_0}}(S,\mathbb C)\neq0.
\]
The first condition has already identified $T$. The second is nonzero
because $\rho$ is distinguished and $\nu|_{H_d}=1$. Since the orbit is
good, the third condition is also nonzero. Using $S\simeq\pi_0$ gives
$ \operatorname{Hom}_{H_{n_0}}(\pi_0,\mathbb C)\neq0.
$
Thus
\[
   \pi\simeq
   \delta_L(\rho)\times\delta_{L-1}(\rho)\times\pi_0
   =\mathcal B_{L-1}(\rho)\times\pi_0,
\]
with $\pi_0$ tempered and distinguished, completing the rank reduction.
head: environment

label: thm:block-rank-reduction
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{thm:block-rank-reduction}
Let $\rho\in\mathcal D_d$, let $m\ge1$, and let
$\pi_0\in\operatorname{Irr}(G_{n_0})$ be tempered. Put
\[
   \Pi
   =\mathcal B_m(\rho)\times\pi_0
   =\delta_{m+1}(\rho)\times\delta_m(\rho)\times\pi_0,
\]
and assume that $\delta_{m+1}(\rho)$ has maximal length among the factors
on the $\rho$-line. If $\Pi$ is $H_n$-distinguished, then $\pi_0$ is
$H_{n_0}$-distinguished.
head: environment
name: Rank reduction for an elementary block

title: Proof
body_md:
Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:rank-reduction} with $L=m+1$ and
$\sigma=\delta_m(\rho)\times\pi_0$. The theorem removes the elementary
block $\mathcal B_m(\rho)$ and gives
\[
   \operatorname{Hom}_{H_{n_0}}(\pi_0,\mathbb C)\neq0.
\]
head: environment

label: thm:general-converse
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:general-converse}
Let $\pi\in\operatorname{Irr}(G_n)$ be  an irreducible tempered representation. If
$
   \operatorname{Hom}_{H_n}(\pi,\mathbb C)\neq0,
$
then
\[ \pi
   \simeq
   \mathcal B_{m_1}(\rho_1)
   \times\cdots\times
   \mathcal B_{m_s}(\rho_s),\]
where $\rho_i\in\mathcal D$ and $m_i\ge0$.
head: environment
name: General converse

title: Proof
body_md:
We induct on the number of unitary discrete-series factors in the tempered
support of $\pi$. Choose a supercuspidal line and a factor
$\delta_L(\rho)$ of maximal length on that line, and place it first.
Proposition~\ref{prop:distinguished-cuspidal-support} shows that $\rho$ is
distinguished, and Theorem~\ref{thm:rank-reduction} gives the corresponding
reduction.

If $L=1$, Theorem~\ref{thm:rank-reduction}\textup{(i)} gives
$ \pi\simeq\mathcal B_0(\rho)\times\pi_0
$
with $\pi_0$ tempered and distinguished. If $L\ge2$, part \textup{(ii)}
gives
$ \pi\simeq\mathcal B_{L-1}(\rho)\times\pi_0
$
with $\pi_0$ again tempered and distinguished. In either case the number
of discrete-series factors strictly decreases. Applying the induction
hypothesis to $\pi_0$ gives the required product of elementary blocks.
head: environment

label: thm:main-classification
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:main-classification}
Let $\pi\in\operatorname{Irr}(G_n)$ be an irreducible tempered representation. Then
\[
   \operatorname{Hom}_{H_n}(\pi,\mathbb C)\neq0
\]
if and only if
\[  \pi
   \simeq
   \mathcal B_{m_1}(\rho_1)
   \times\cdots\times
   \mathcal B_{m_s}(\rho_s),
   \]
with $\rho_i\in\mathcal D$ and $m_i\ge0$.
head: environment
name: Prasad's revised tempered conjecture

title: Proof
body_md:
The ``only if'' direction is Theorem~\ref{thm:general-converse}. For the
``if'' direction, every $\mathcal B_m(\rho)$ is distinguished by
Theorem~\ref{thm:Bm-general}, with $m=0$ interpreted as a distinguished
supercuspidal singleton, and arbitrary products are distinguished by the
hereditary property.
head: environment
